paper.title: Efficient Uncoupled Learning Dynamics with $\tilde{O}\!\left(T^{-1/4}\right)$ Last-Iterate Convergence in Bilinear Saddle-Point Problems over Convex Sets under Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Last-iterate convergence in bilinear saddle-point problems over compact convex sets under bandit feedback (self-play, uncoupled)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Two-player zero-sum game (learning in games / self-play); the guarantee is last-iterate convergence to a Nash equilibrium, not a bandit regret or identification objective.
unmapped: Two-player zero-sum bilinear game <x, A y>, both players run the uncoupled algorithm in self-play
Objective: the round-k iterate (x_k, y_k) is an eps_k-approximate Nash equilibrium (last-iterate convergence)
<x, A y> in [-1,1] for all x in X, y in Y
Players do not observe opponent actions, action set or dimension
settings.definition_quote: In each round $k$, the row player selects $x_k \in \mathcal{X}$ and the column player selects $y_k \in \mathcal{Y}$. They then receive standard bandit feedback in the form of $\langle x_k, Ay_k \rangle$ and $-\langle x_k, Ay_k \rangle$, respectively.

algorithms.name: Last-iterate algorithm under bandit feedback (phased OFTRL with ellipsoid regularizer and volumetric-spanner exploration)

bound.regime: for every k >= 1, simultaneously, with probability at least 1-delta

symbols.n_dim: dimension of the row player's action set X in R^n
symbols.m_dim: dimension of the column player's action set Y in R^m
symbols.eps_k: Nash-equilibrium approximation level of the round-k iterate (x_k, y_k)

conditions: X and Y compact convex with span(X)=R^n, span(Y)=R^m
<x, A y> in [-1,1] for all x in X, y in Y
tuning: exploration distribution uniform over a volumetric-spanner-type subset with sup x^T V^{-1} x <= 2n^2

source.label: thm:main_theorem
source.quote: Consider a two-player zero-sum game with action sets $\mathcal{X} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m$, where both $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ are convex and compact. Let $(x_k, y_k)$ denote the iterates generated by the two players running Algorithm~1 with step size $\eta = \tfrac{1}{6}$ in each round $k$. Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for every $k \geq 1$, the iterate $(x_k,y_k)$ is an $\varepsilon_k$-approximate Nash equilibrium, where $\varepsilon_k = \mathrm{poly}(n,m,\log(k/\delta)) \, k^{-1/4}$.

results.notes: The theorem states only poly(n,m,log(k/delta)) k^{-1/4}; the explicit polynomial (n^3+m^3) log k log^{1/4}(8k^2/delta) is from the proof sketch at the end of Section 3. Quantity is the Nash-gap of the last iterate, not regret. Polynomial-time given a linear optimization oracle (Section 4).
